chemistry-killer-02.title: Mixtures and Dissolution Principles
chemistry-killer-02.goal: Analyze the principles of Mixtures and Dissolution Principles and deduce the correct conclusion under given conditions.
chemistry-killer-02.material:
For constant temperature and pressure, hydrogen ($\mathrm{H_2}$) and oxygen ($\mathrm{O_2}$) dey react to form water vapour ($\mathrm{H_2O}$(g)). Dem react different gas mixtures completely and measure di total volume of gas for di same temperature and pressure as follows (all di water vapour dey gas state).
(I) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 30 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL → total 35 mL after reaction
(II) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 20 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL → total 30 mL after reaction
Dem react 60 mL of mixed gas of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ completely for di same temperature and pressure, di total volume of gas after di reaction na 45 mL, and di only gas wey remain na $\mathrm{O_2}$ ($\mathrm{H_2}$ no remain). Which one correctly match, in order, di volume of $\mathrm{H_2}$ before di reaction and di volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey remain after di reaction?
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.prompt:
For constant temperature and pressure, hydrogen ($\mathrm{H_2}$) and oxygen ($\mathrm{O_2}$) dey react to form water vapour ($\mathrm{H_2O}$(g)). Dem react different gas mixtures completely and measure di total volume of gas for di same temperature and pressure as follows (all di water vapour dey gas state).
(I) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 30 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL → total 35 mL after reaction
(II) $\mathrm{H_2}$ 20 mL + $\mathrm{O_2}$ 20 mL → total 30 mL after reaction
Dem react 60 mL of mixed gas of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ completely for di same temperature and pressure, di total volume of gas after di reaction na 45 mL, and di only gas wey remain na $\mathrm{O_2}$ ($\mathrm{H_2}$ no remain). Which one correctly match, in order, di volume of $\mathrm{H_2}$ before di reaction and di volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey remain after di reaction?
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: Check di volume ratio from (I) and (II). (II): H2 20 mL react with O2 10 mL to form H2O 20 mL, O2 10 mL remain → total 30 mL. (I): H2 30 mL react with O2 15 mL to form H2O 30 mL, O2 5 mL remain → total 35 mL. So di reaction volume ratio $\mathrm{H_2:O_2:H_2O(g)} = 2:1:2$.
Step 2: Before di reaction na 60 mL and after na 45 mL, so di decrease na 15 mL. For di reaction, every 3 volumes of gas become 2 volumes so e lose 1 volume, and di volume wey reduce = volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey react, so $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey react = 15 mL.
Step 3: Because no $\mathrm{H_2}$ remain, all di H2 react: 15×2 = 30 mL. H2O(g) wey form = 30 mL. Di total after reaction na 45 mL, so $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey remain = 45 − 30 = 15 mL. $\mathrm{O_2}$ before di reaction = 15 + 15 = 30 mL, and di sum 30 + 30 = 60 mL match.
Answer: 30 mL, 15 mL (b).
chemistry-killer-02.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
chemistry-killer-02.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.hint.0: For $\mathrm{2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O(g)}$, 3 volumes of gas become 2 volumes, so di decrease in volume before and after di reaction = volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey react.
chemistry-killer-02.s.s1.hint.1: Decrease = 60 − 45 = 15 mL = volume of $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey react. Because all di $\mathrm{H_2}$ react, $\mathrm{H_2}$ wey react = 15×2 = 30 mL, and $\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$ wey form = 30 mL.
